answer: Terrace inventory bond: each identity stocks a terrace stall with velvet-sealed lots, locks 70 credits, logs serials in a public atlas. Each epoch an auditor re-counts one stall against the atlas; a shortfall or borrowed velvet seal burns the bond. First stall costs 45, kth 45+4(k-1); 1,000 fakes pay 2,043,000 plus 70,000 locked vs 40,000 pool. A rented-lot ring fails: one seal cannot cover two stalls. Honest agents pay 45 once and keep selling.
